boundary: Privacy / Confidentiality alone would be right if the client had not stated a prior-notice and review requirement for any recording, so that recording without consent prompts were only a privacy intrusion and not also a consent/compliance breach.
factor: Meeting recording armed with consent prompts disabled, contrary to a counterparty's stated pre-recording requirement.
note: fact_layer correct; the assessor quoted both the disabled consent prompt and the client's notice requirement but folded the breach into privacy, giving one label instead of the gold two.
